PDEP — Governed Self-Service Product Development & Evolution (Family-Neutral)
Shift Creation Power Left — From Requesting Products to Creating Products
Product Owners / Symbiants create and evolve Products using governed HDIP capabilities across applicable Planes.
The seven experience groupings below are illustrative — not an independent canonical lifecycle or numbered Product-family stage model.
Creates, owns and continuously evolves the Product
• Purpose and value • Problem / opportunity • Initial scope • Success measures
• Select Product family • Define characteristics • Specify metadata • Model structure • Quality expectations
• Resolve dependencies • Policy and compliance • Compatibility checks • Applicable authorities
• Assemble components • Compile and validate • Generate artifacts • Prepare for publication
• Qualification evidence • Assurance evidence • Outstanding decisions • Indicative cost & impact • Realization readiness
• Register and publish • Deploy applicable parts • Enable governed use • Make discoverable
• Observe usage • Capture outcomes • Evolve and improve • Re-enter as needed
Continuous Improvement — Re-enter at Earliest Materially Affected Stage
Realized Outcomes Usage · performance · trust signals
Value & Economic Impact Indicative and observed economic evidence
Evolution & Re-entry Enhancements · new versions · extended scope
PDEP is a governed cross-Plane self-service experience — NOT a mandatory project or delivery pipeline.
DATA PRODUCT PROFILE — Canonical Specialization: Stage 0 to Stage 10
Stage 8 compilation outputs: RRG · HPD · SYNCTX (conditional) · RGB · Realization Plan · Blueprint Binding · Compilation Record
Data Stage 0–10 is NOT the universal lifecycle for Information, Intelligence/AI or Compound Products.
X1–X9 — Cross-Cutting Overlays (Applicable Across All PDEP Responsibilities)
Enables realization; does not establish semantics, Product qualification, policy authority or enterprise accountability.
• Product development is a governed self-service experience led by the Product Owner / Symbiant.
• HDIP provides engineering, compilation, validation, realization and publication automation.
• Not a requester-to-delivery-team model; no mandatory intermediary.
• PDEP spans HDIP Planes; it is not another Plane.
• A lifecycle is not a mandatory synchronous runtime pipeline.
• Defines intent, value, scope and success measures.
• Uses self-service capabilities with guided governance.
• Engineering, compilation, validation, realization and publication automation.
• Indicative cost and economic impact decision support.
• Enables ongoing evolution and consumption hand-off.
• Compound: applicable constituents and Product authority.
• Do not impose Data stages on other families.
• Indicative cost and economic impact support decisions throughout the lifecycle.
• Funding, budget authority, approval workflows and investment automation are enterprise-specific.
• HDIP prescribes no funding or investment governance model.
• Source: M10 PDEP and M15 Reference Views.
• P1–P5 participation varies by family and change.
• P3 Data, Information and Intelligence stay distinct.
• G0 / Spec A / Spec C are presentation projections.
• No universal topology or automatic conformance.
